cards.front: What are the primary distinctions between functional overreaching (FOR), nonfunctional overreaching (NFOR), and overtraining syndrome (OTS)?
cards.back:
• Functional Overreaching (FOR): Short-term performance drop followed by supercompensation post-tapering (recovery in days to weeks).
  • Nonfunctional Overreaching (NFOR): Extreme overreaching causing performance stagnation/decrease lasting weeks to months.
  • Overtraining Syndrome (OTS): Severe, prolonged maladaptation of biological, neurochemical, and hormonal mechanisms lasting 6 months or beyond.

cards.front: How do sympathetic and parasympathetic overtraining syndromes differ in their onset, symptoms, and target athlete populations?
cards.back:
• Sympathetic OTS: Elevated resting sympathetic activity, predominates early in younger speed/power athletes (insomnia, restlessness, elevated resting HR).
  • Parasympathetic OTS: Elevated resting/exercise parasympathetic activity, predominates in endurance sports, representing end-stage exhaustion with systemic endocrine suppression.

cards.front: In the short-term NFOR squat study by Fry et al. (8 sets at 95% 1RM for 6 consecutive days), which performance metrics decreased and which was preserved?
cards.back: The protocol caused nonspecific performance decrements in isokinetic torque production, sprint times, and agility times, while 1RM strength was preserved.

cards.front: What performance outcome occurred when subjects performed 10 sets of 1RM squats daily for 7 days (Fry et al., 1998)?
cards.back: A significant decrease of >9.9 lb (>4.5 kg) in 1RM squat strength occurred in 73% of subjects, demonstrating substantial individual variation in overreaching tolerance.

cards.front: How do endocrine responses differ between volume-related overtraining and intensity-related overtraining?
cards.back:
• Volume-related OTS: Increases resting cortisol and decreases resting total/free testosterone and luteinizing hormone (LH).
  • Intensity-related OTS: Produces no significant changes in resting concentrations of testosterone, free testosterone, cortisol, or growth hormone.

cards.front: What is the physiological interpretation of the resting plasma testosterone-to-cortisol ratio in training load monitoring?
cards.back: The ratio reflects the actual physiological strain of training (anabolic/catabolic balance), decreasing with heightened training intensity and volume, but serves as a strain marker rather than a diagnostic tool for OTS.

cards.front: What neuroendocrine progression occurs in highly trained athletes during nonfunctional overreaching according to Meeusen et al.?
cards.back: Athletes initially experience an intense, hypersensitive sympathetic hormone surge, followed by suppression of pituitary hormone release (ACTH, GH, LH, FSH) due to receptor downregulation and pituitary exhaustion.

cards.front: Why are psychological alterations monitored via the Profile of Mood States (POMS) critical for identifying overtraining?
cards.back: Psychological shifts—including decreased vigor and motivation alongside increased tension, depression, anger, fatigue, and confusion—often manifest before measurable physical performance decrements occur.

cards.front: What primary exercise prescription mistakes contribute to the development of anaerobic overtraining syndrome?
cards.back:
• Excessive rate of progressive overload: Increasing volume or intensity too rapidly over weeks or months.
  • Excessive volume and intensity pairing: Combining heavy loads with high set volume and high frequency without adequate recovery rest.

cards.front: What percentage of overtrained survey subjects participated in high-velocity/high-force sports, and how do their symptoms present?
cards.back: A survey showed that 77% of overtrained athletes were involved in sports requiring high strength, speed, or coordination, displaying sympathetic overtraining symptoms rather than parasympathetic endurance symptoms.
